Handy reads visible on-screen text and the UI tree so the assistant can answer questions about what you see and point at the right button. If you separately enable Tap-for-me, Handy can tap or scroll only after you confirm that exact action on screen. Handy blocks sensitive apps and you can turn this off at any time in Settings.
on-screen AI assistant overlay that must remain visible across apps

Handy is an on-screen AI assistant. When you ask a question, Handy reads visible on-screen text via the Android Accessibility service and may capture the active window, then sends your message plus that context to Anthropic (Claude) over HTTPS using your own API key. Optional web-search tools send queries to Brave, Jina, and the public GitHub API only when you enable them in Settings. Tap-for-me is a separate opt-in after Accessibility is enabled: Handy can tap or scroll only after you confirm that exact action on screen, and sensitive apps are blocked. No data is sent to our servers — Handy has none. You can decline any permission and Handy will run in a reduced mode.

Tap-for-me lets Handy tap, scroll, or type ordinary text into the item it just pointed at. It is optional, versioned consent on top of Accessibility access.
After Buddy lands on a target, Handy shows an overlay confirmation sheet. No tap, scroll, or typing runs unless you approve that specific action.
Banking, payments, password managers, secure windows, stale screens, and low-confidence targets are denied before the confirmation sheet appears.
Settings includes a Tap-for-me toggle, a one-hour panic mute, and a revoke action that clears this consent immediately.

Brave powers general web search, Jina Reader fetches and summarises pages, GitHub searches public repos. Jina + GitHub keys are optional — they raise rate limits.
